options.label: B
options.text: Validating unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens and using SameSite cookie flags on state-changing requests

options.label: C
options.text: Mandating password complexity rules that enforce credential changes every thirty days for active users

options.label: D
options.text: Encoding all incoming form parameters into base64 strings before processing them in application controllers

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: CSRF protection requires unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens tied to the user's session that third-party sites cannot read or guess, alongside SameSite cookie attributes.

questions.questionText: What underlying microarchitectural processor mechanism enables Spectre speculative execution side-channel attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: Branch predictors executing instructions speculatively past bounds checks and leaving cache timing traces

options.label: B
options.text: Improper cyclic redundancy checks on L1 data cache lines during asynchronous direct memory access

options.label: C
options.text: Memory management unit page table fragmentation allowing unprivileged user space to read kernel frames

options.label: D
options.text: Hardware thermal throttling desynchronizing clock cycles between physical processor execution cores

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Spectre exploits speculative execution where CPUs predict branch targets and execute code before bounds checks complete. When squashed, cache state changes persist and leak data via timing attacks.

questions.questionText: In modern binary exploitation, what is the primary purpose of Return-Oriented Programming (ROP)?

options.label: A
options.text: To execute kernel shellcode by directly corrupting the hardware interrupt descriptor table from user space

options.label: B
options.text: To defeat Address Space Layout Randomization by brute-forcing fixed virtual memory offsets in running processes

options.label: C
options.text: To accelerate reverse engineering by translating raw assembly opcodes into structured control flow graphs

options.label: D
options.text: To defeat Data Execution Prevention (W^X / DEP) by chaining existing executable instruction sequences ending in ret

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: When memory regions are marked non-executable (DEP/NX), ROP circumvents this by reusing existing snippets of executable binary code ('gadgets') ending in return instructions to build arbitrary logic.

questions.questionText: How is Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) typically defeated during exploit development?

options.label: A
options.text: By corrupting the system real-time clock to desynchronize kernel random number generator initialization

options.label: B
options.text: By transmitting high-volume ICMP echo requests to exhaust kernel socket buffer memory allocations

options.label: C
options.text: By modifying system security limits in user space configuration files to exceed kernel allocation limits

options.label: D
options.text: By using an information leak vulnerability that reveals a kernel pointer to calculate the randomized base offset

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: KASLR randomizes the base memory location of kernel code. Attackers leverage an information disclosure bug that leaks a known kernel function pointer to calculate the base slide offset.

questions.questionText: In Kubernetes, which container configuration enables an attacker to perform a host node breakout?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploying a container image built on minimal Alpine Linux rather than an enterprise Linux distribution

options.label: B
options.text: Attaching a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler that adjusts pod replica counts based on CPU utilization metrics

options.label: C
options.text: Running in privileged mode with hostPID and hostNetwork enabled or the host filesystem mounted read-write

options.label: D
options.text: Configuring the pod to resolve DNS through cluster CoreDNS services rather than node-local caching daemons

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Privileged containers disable Linux cgroup and namespace isolation. Access to host devices or the root filesystem allows escape via chroot, device access, or cgroup release agent manipulation.

questions.questionText: What condition permits an attacker to perform a Blind Time-Based SQL Injection attack against an API?

options.label: A
options.text: The application communicates with the database over an unencrypted network connection without TLS verification

options.label: B
options.text: The endpoint returns identical responses regardless of query results, but evaluates injected delay functions

options.label: C
options.text: The database connection pool suffers from connection starvation due to unindexed queries on large tables

options.label: D
options.text: The database server exposes detailed error stack traces and internal schema definitions in HTTP 500 responses

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: When an application leaks no data or differential error messages, an attacker injects conditional time-delay commands (like pg_sleep or WAITFOR DELAY) to infer data bit-by-bit from response times.

questions.questionText: In SAML 2.0 implementations, what design flaw enables XML Signature Wrapping (XSW) attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: A mismatch between the XML structure used during signature canonicalization and that interpreted by the app

options.label: B
options.text: A mismatch between the XML node validated by the signature verifier and the node consumed by business logic

options.label: C
options.text: A mismatch between namespace resolution during signature verification and resolution during assertion processing

options.label: D
options.text: A mismatch between schema validation of the assertion and resolution of referenced signed element identifiers

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: XSW exploits architectural discrepancies where signature verification validates an intact assertion, while business logic retrieves user claims from an unsigned, wrapped element elsewhere in the DOM.

questions.questionText: What cryptographic flaw made WPA2's 4-way handshake vulnerable to Key Reinstallation Attacks (KRACK)?

options.label: A
options.text: The wireless controller generating predictable initialization vectors during RC4 stream cipher encapsulation

options.label: B
options.text: The authentication server transmitting the master pre-shared key in plaintext beacon frames during discovery

options.label: C
options.text: The client reinstalling an in-use pairwise key upon receiving retransmitted Message 3, resetting the packet counter

options.label: D
options.text: The access point using weak Diffie-Hellman primes that allow pre-computation attacks against session keys

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: KRACK exploits Message 3 retransmission. When re-received, vulnerable clients reinstall the already active PTK and reset its transmit replay counter (nonce), enabling keystream reuse attacks.

questions.questionText: Why is ML-KEM (Kyber) categorized as lattice-based post-quantum cryptography?

options.label: A
options.text: It utilizes super-singular elliptic curve isogenies requiring exponential classical resources to compute path morphisms

options.label: B
options.text: It generates symmetric one-time pads derived from cosmic background radiation sensors embedded in security modules

options.label: C
options.text: It employs quantum key distribution channels that leverage photon entanglement to detect eavesdropping on optical lines

options.label: D
options.text: Its security relies on high-dimensional lattice vector problems that cannot be solved efficiently by Shor's algorithm

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: ML-KEM security reduces to the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) problem over high-dimensional lattices, which resists both classical algorithms and quantum attacks based on Shor's algorithm.

questions.questionText: In eBPF security observability tooling, how can a root-privileged adversary attempt to blind kernel telemetry?

options.label: A
options.text: By adjusting system timezone configurations to create clock drift between worker nodes and the control plane

options.label: B
options.text: By modifying userspace /etc/resolv.conf configuration files to redirect internal DNS queries to external resolvers

options.label: C
options.text: By installing unapproved compilers on the host worker node to trigger local static binary analysis warnings

options.label: D
options.text: By detaching kernel tracepoints via bpf syscalls or flooding the ring buffer to induce massive unlogged event drops

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: An adversary with root or CAP_BPF can interact directly with the bpf() syscall to detach attached probes, corrupt BPF maps, or generate high-volume synthetic events to overflow ring buffers.

questions.questionText: Which defense mechanism specifically protects cloud instance metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) against SSRF?

options.label: A
options.text: Enforcing IMDSv2 requiring session-oriented PUT requests with signed token headers alongside strict egress filtering

options.label: B
options.text: Configuring public DNS records to map internal private IP subnets to corporate reverse proxy load balancers

options.label: C
options.text: Enforcing multi-factor authentication on all administrative SSH connections established to worker compute nodes

options.label: D
options.text: Encoding all outbound HTTP request bodies into base64 strings before transmitting them over network gateways

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: IMDSv2 requires clients to first execute a PUT request to generate a session token (which standard SSRF vectors cannot easily forge) before querying metadata, and sets token hop limits to block proxies.

questions.questionText: How does the JavaScript Event Loop coordinate the execution of microtasks (Promises) versus macrotasks (setTimeout)?

options.label: A
options.text: Microtasks are cancelled automatically if a new macrotask arrives in the queue within five milliseconds

options.label: B
options.text: Microtasks execute after all pending macrotasks finish, right before the browser rendering frame begins

options.label: C
options.text: Macrotasks and microtasks execute concurrently on separate operating system background threads

options.label: D
options.text: The microtask queue is completely drained after each synchronous call stack completion before the next macrotask runs

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: At the end of each task on the call stack, the JavaScript runtime completely exhausts the microtask queue (Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask, MutationObservers) before picking the next macrotask (setTimeout, I/O).

questions.questionText: In React, what problem does the useCallback hook specifically solve?

options.label: A
options.text: It converts client component state mutations into server actions executed directly on backend workers

options.label: B
options.text: It memoizes a callback function definition between renders, maintaining reference equality for optimized child components

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically captures unhandled JavaScript runtime exceptions thrown during component render lifecycles

options.label: D
options.text: It memoizes heavy synchronous computational calculations to prevent them from executing on the main thread

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: In React, functions are recreated on every render. useCallback memoizes the function instance based on a dependency array, preserving reference equality (===) so that child components wrapped in React.memo skip unnecessary re-renders.

questions.questionText: What distinguishes Server-Side Rendering (SSR) from Static Site Generation (SSG) in frameworks like Next.js?

options.label: A
options.text: SSR eliminates the need for client hydration, while SSG requires downloading complete server database drivers

options.label: B
options.text: SSR renders HTML dynamically on each user request, while SSG pre-renders HTML pages ahead of time at build time

options.label: C
options.text: SSR cannot fetch data from external REST APIs, while SSG dynamically connects to live WebSocket feeds

options.label: D
options.text: SSR is executed inside the user's browser, while SSG requires continuous Node.js server runtimes in production

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: SSR generates HTML dynamically per request on the server (suitable for personalized, real-time data). SSG generates HTML once during compilation, allowing pages to be cached globally on CDNs for near-instant delivery.

questions.questionText: How does Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) evaluate whether a cross-origin HTTP request is permitted?

options.label: A
options.text: The web server forces the connecting client browser to restart and clear all stored session cookies

options.label: B
options.text: The client browser verifies that the destination server IP address belongs to the same local subnet range

options.label: C
options.text: The browser sends an OPTIONS preflight request to verify that server response headers allow the origin and method

options.label: D
options.text: The operating system firewall inspects the application process signature against global DNS records

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: For non-simple requests, browsers dispatch an HTTP OPTIONS preflight call with Origin and Access-Control-Request-* headers. The browser checks if the server responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin matching the calling domain before proceeding.

questions.questionText: An e-commerce search bar triggers an API call on every keystroke, causing severe backend query overload. What is the solution?

options.label: A
options.text: Convert all search queries into synchronous XMLHttpRequest calls executed directly on the main thread

options.label: B
options.text: Store the entire product catalog database in the user's browser cookie storage header partition

options.label: C
options.text: Disable browser JavaScript and force the search input to submit a standard multi-part form post

options.label: D
options.text: Implement a debounce function that waits for the user to pause typing before dispatching the network request

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Debouncing delays the function execution until a specified delay has elapsed since the last event (e.g. 300ms after user stops typing). This collapses 20 rapid keystrokes into a single optimized network query.

questions.questionText: What role does optimistic UI update play in modern full-stack web applications?

options.label: A
options.text: It forces the client browser to refresh the entire webpage immediately following every user interaction

options.label: B
options.text: It caches all user modifications on the server for twenty-four hours before committing them to the database

options.label: C
options.text: It updates the client interface immediately assuming the mutation succeeds, rolling back if the server fails

options.label: D
options.text: It converts frontend state changes into binary WebAssembly instructions to bypass network validation

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Optimistic updates immediately render expected state changes in the UI (e.g. toggling a 'like' button) without waiting for server round-trip latency, rolling back to the previous state with a notification if the network request errors.

questions.questionText: How does code splitting improve the Initial Page Load performance of a large web application?

options.label: A
options.text: It minifies HTML whitespace so that CSS files are executed directly by the operating system kernel

options.label: B
options.text: It replaces all external library dependencies with native browser DOM manipulation equivalents

options.label: C
options.text: It splits database queries across multiple relational tables during server-side template compilation

options.label: D
options.text: It breaks the bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand, reducing the initial JavaScript parsed by the browser

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Rather than shipping a monolithic multi-megabyte bundle, bundlers split code by route or dynamic import (React.lazy), loading only the JavaScript required for the initial route and fetching other chunks lazily.

questions.questionText: Why is setting 'HttpOnly' and 'SameSite=Lax' flags on session cookies considered standard security practice?

options.label: A
options.text: HttpOnly blocks client-side script access mitigating XSS theft, while SameSite restricts cross-site CSRF delivery

options.label: B
options.text: HttpOnly compresses cookie data using gzip, while SameSite encrypts cookies with local public key certificates

options.label: C
options.text: HttpOnly forces the browser to delete session cookies after sixty seconds of inactivity across user tabs

options.label: D
options.text: HttpOnly restricts cookie transmission exclusively to internal private subnets without public internet access

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: HttpOnly prevents document.cookie access from JavaScript, thwarting cookie theft via XSS. SameSite=Lax/Strict prevents the browser from sending the cookie in cross-site requests, mitigating CSRF attacks.

questions.questionText: What problem occurs when multiple clients update the same database record simultaneously without concurrency controls?

options.label: A
options.text: The database server immediately terminates all client TCP sockets and triggers automatic index rebuilds

options.label: B
options.text: The Lost Update anomaly, where the later write unintentionally overwrites changes committed by the earlier write

options.label: C
options.text: The operating system converts the relational database tables into uncompressed plain text CSV archives

options.label: D
options.text: All future client read queries on that table return HTTP 404 Not Found status errors indefinitely

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: In a lost update, Client A and Client B read state X simultaneously. Client A updates X and saves. Client B updates X based on the original read and saves, silently overwriting A's modifications without knowing. Optimistic concurrency (version checks) resolves this.

questions.questionText: How does the browser's Service Worker API enable Progressive Web App (PWA) offline capability?

options.label: A
options.text: By compiling web application TypeScript files into native mobile Android APK files in the background

options.label: B
options.text: By generating synthetic Wi-Fi connections that simulate internet availability using cellular radio hardware

options.label: C
options.text: By embedding a lightweight headless relational database inside the browser's GPU rendering pipeline

options.label: D
options.text: By acting as a client-side network proxy that intercepts fetch requests and serves cached responses from CacheStorage

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Service Workers run in a background thread and intercept network fetch events. When offline, the worker intercepts requests and returns matching cached responses from the CacheStorage API, enabling full offline operation.

questions.questionText: How does a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack execute in a target web application?

options.label: A
options.text: By manipulating HTTP caching headers to store sensitive authentication cookies in intermediate proxies

options.label: B
options.text: By injecting untrusted client script into web application pages that executes in other users' browsers

options.label: C
options.text: By corrupting browser DNS cache records to redirect legitimate API requests to adversary endpoints

options.label: D
options.text: By appending SQL syntax into URL parameters to dump user password hashes from the relational database

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: XSS occurs when an application includes untrusted user input without context-aware encoding, leading the browser to execute injected scripts in the security context of the user.

questions.questionText: Which HTTP header is specifically designed to restrict where scripts, styles, and assets can load from?

options.label: A
options.text: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), declaring authorized sources from which scripts and resources may be loaded

options.label: B
options.text: Access-Control-Allow-Origin, controlling which external web domains can access cross-origin API responses

options.label: C
options.text: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), enforcing encrypted HTTPS communication for all domain connections

options.label: D
options.text: X-Frame-Options, preventing malicious sites from rendering the target page inside hidden frame overlays

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Content-Security-Policy (CSP) allows site operators to restrict the origins of executable scripts, stylesheets, and media, effectively neutralizing unauthorized inline script execution.

questions.questionText: Why are adaptive algorithms like Argon2 and bcrypt preferred over fast hashes like SHA-256 for passwords?

options.label: A
options.text: They incorporate configurable work factors and memory hardness to resist GPU and ASIC brute-force attacks

options.label: B
options.text: They generate variable-length outputs that eliminate hash collision vulnerabilities across large datasets

options.label: C
options.text: They eliminate the need for random cryptographic salts by computing deterministic seed values

options.label: D
options.text: They use asymmetric key pairs requiring separate public and private keys to verify password matches

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Fast hash functions like SHA-256 are engineered for speed, allowing billions of guesses per second on GPUs. Adaptive functions introduce computational work factors and memory demands to thwart hardware cracking.

questions.questionText: A security analyst observes high volumes of outbound DNS queries for random hex subdomains. What is the threat?

options.label: A
options.text: DNS tunneling and data exfiltration encoding unauthorized data within sequential lookup query labels

options.label: B
options.text: Dynamic DNS client registration updating external public IP address bindings following lease renewal

options.label: C
options.text: Authoritative name server zone synchronization transferring DNS resource records to secondary servers

options.label: D
options.text: Standard browser cache prefetching optimizing domain name resolution latency for anticipated user clicks

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: DNS tunneling encapsulates non-DNS traffic or stolen data inside DNS queries (e.g. data.attacker.com), bypassing standard egress firewall rules that leave port 53 open.

questions.questionText: What is the most robust defense against SQL Injection vulnerabilities in modern web applications?

options.label: A
options.text: Restricting database connections to communicate exclusively over mutually authenticated TLS sockets

options.label: B
options.text: Storing database credentials in encrypted configuration files rather than hardcoding them in source

options.label: C
options.text: Filtering incoming request parameters with regular expressions to remove single quotes and semicolons

options.label: D
options.text: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) that separate user input from SQL command structure

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Parameterized queries ensure the database driver treats user input strictly as data values, preventing user input from altering the compiled SQL query syntax.

questions.questionText: What security advantage does network micro-segmentation provide inside a corporate infrastructure?

options.label: A
options.text: It removes the operational requirement to apply operating system security updates on internal servers

options.label: B
options.text: It isolates workloads into discrete zones, preventing adversaries from moving laterally if a host is breached

options.label: C
options.text: It automates edge router failover by dynamically re-routing external traffic across redundant gateways

options.label: D
options.text: It increases raw packet throughput by bypassing perimeter firewall inspection for internal subnet traffic

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Micro-segmentation restricts communication between workloads according to granular policies, limiting an attacker's ability to move laterally across an internal network.

questions.questionText: If an API verifies JWTs without enforcing the signature algorithm (accepting 'alg: none'), what attack occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: Attackers can bypass Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) preflight validation on protected endpoints

options.label: B
options.text: Attackers can forge arbitrary claims and tamper with tokens without needing a valid cryptographic signature

options.label: C
options.text: Attackers can cause server denial of service by triggering recursive cryptographic verification routines

options.label: D
options.text: Attackers can force identity servers to issue refresh tokens with permanent operational validity periods

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: If a server blindly honors 'alg: none', an attacker can modify the token payload (e.g. elevating role to admin) and strip the signature, gaining unauthorized privileges.

questions.questionText: What is the primary security goal of implementing the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?

options.label: A
options.text: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is necessary, minimizing potential blast radius

options.label: B
options.text: To eliminate the need for administrative accounts by delegating all operational tasks to background services

options.label: C
options.text: To enforce automatic session logout whenever an authenticated user remains inactive for fifteen minutes

options.label: D
options.text: To reduce cloud infrastructure billing costs by removing unused role-based access control assignments

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Least Privilege dictates that users, processes, and systems should hold only the bare minimum permissions required to perform their functions, containing damage from compromise.

questions.questionText: How does Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling improve upon traditional revocation checking?

options.label: A
options.text: It replaces asymmetric public key infrastructure with symmetric shared secret keys across web browsers

options.label: B
options.text: It embeds the revocation status of all public certificates directly into local operating system trust stores

options.label: C
options.text: It allows web clients to query multiple Certificate Authorities concurrently to verify root trust chains

options.label: D
options.text: It allows web servers to deliver timestamped, CA-signed revocation proof during the TLS handshake

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: OCSP Stapling delegates status retrieval to the web server, which caches a signed OCSP response and presents it to connecting clients during TLS negotiation, enhancing speed and privacy.

options.label: A

options.text: By corrupting browser DNS cache records to redirect legitimate API requests to adversary endpoints

options.label: D
options.text: By injecting untrusted client script into web application pages that executes in other users' browsers

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: XSS occurs when an application includes untrusted user input without context-aware encoding, leading the browser to execute injected scripts in the security context of the user.

questions.questionText: Which HTTP header is specifically designed to restrict where scripts, styles, and assets can load from?

options.label: A
options.text: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), declaring authorized sources from which scripts and resources may be loaded

options.label: B
options.text: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), enforcing encrypted HTTPS communication for all domain connections

options.label: C
options.text: X-Frame-Options, preventing malicious sites from rendering the target page inside hidden frame overlays

options.label: D
options.text: Access-Control-Allow-Origin, controlling which external web domains can access cross-origin API responses

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Content-Security-Policy (CSP) allows site operators to restrict the origins of executable scripts, stylesheets, and media, effectively neutralizing unauthorized inline script execution.

questions.questionText: Why are adaptive algorithms like Argon2 and bcrypt preferred over fast hashes like SHA-256 for passwords?

options.label: A
options.text: They incorporate configurable work factors and memory hardness to resist GPU and ASIC brute-force attacks

options.label: B
options.text: They use asymmetric key pairs requiring separate public and private keys to verify password matches

options.label: C
options.text: They eliminate the need for random cryptographic salts by computing deterministic seed values

options.label: D
options.text: They generate variable-length outputs that eliminate hash collision vulnerabilities across large datasets

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Fast hash functions like SHA-256 are engineered for speed, allowing billions of guesses per second on GPUs. Adaptive functions introduce computational work factors and memory demands to thwart hardware cracking.

questions.questionText: A security analyst observes high volumes of outbound DNS queries for random hex subdomains. What is the threat?

options.label: A
options.text: DNS tunneling and data exfiltration encoding unauthorized data within sequential lookup query labels

options.label: B
options.text: Dynamic DNS client registration updating external public IP address bindings following lease renewal

options.label: C
options.text: Standard browser cache prefetching optimizing domain name resolution latency for anticipated user clicks

options.label: D
options.text: Authoritative name server zone synchronization transferring DNS resource records to secondary servers

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: DNS tunneling encapsulates non-DNS traffic or stolen data inside DNS queries (e.g. data.attacker.com), bypassing standard egress firewall rules that leave port 53 open.

questions.questionText: What is the most robust defense against SQL Injection vulnerabilities in modern web applications?

options.label: A
options.text: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) that separate user input from SQL command structure

options.label: B
options.text: Restricting database connections to communicate exclusively over mutually authenticated TLS sockets

options.label: C
options.text: Storing database credentials in encrypted configuration files rather than hardcoding them in source

options.label: D
options.text: Filtering incoming request parameters with regular expressions to remove single quotes and semicolons

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Parameterized queries ensure the database driver treats user input strictly as data values, preventing user input from altering the compiled SQL query syntax.

questions.questionText: What security advantage does network micro-segmentation provide inside a corporate infrastructure?

options.label: A
options.text: It automates edge router failover by dynamically re-routing external traffic across redundant gateways

options.label: B
options.text: It isolates workloads into discrete zones, preventing adversaries from moving laterally if a host is breached

options.label: C
options.text: It removes the operational requirement to apply operating system security updates on internal servers

options.label: D
options.text: It increases raw packet throughput by bypassing perimeter firewall inspection for internal subnet traffic

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Micro-segmentation restricts communication between workloads according to granular policies, limiting an attacker's ability to move laterally across an internal network.

questions.questionText: If an API verifies JWTs without enforcing the signature algorithm (accepting 'alg: none'), what attack occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: Attackers can bypass Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) preflight validation on protected endpoints

options.label: B
options.text: Attackers can force identity servers to issue refresh tokens with permanent operational validity periods

options.label: C
options.text: Attackers can forge arbitrary claims and tamper with tokens without needing a valid cryptographic signature

options.label: D
options.text: Attackers can cause server denial of service by triggering recursive cryptographic verification routines

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: If a server blindly honors 'alg: none', an attacker can modify the token payload (e.g. elevating role to admin) and strip the signature, gaining unauthorized privileges.

questions.questionText: What is the primary security goal of implementing the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?

options.label: A
options.text: To enforce automatic session logout whenever an authenticated user remains inactive for fifteen minutes

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce cloud infrastructure billing costs by removing unused role-based access control assignments

options.label: C
options.text: To eliminate the need for administrative accounts by delegating all operational tasks to background services

options.label: D
options.text: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is necessary, minimizing potential blast radius

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Least Privilege dictates that users, processes, and systems should hold only the bare minimum permissions required to perform their functions, containing damage from compromise.

questions.questionText: How does Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling improve upon traditional revocation checking?

options.label: A
options.text: It embeds the revocation status of all public certificates directly into local operating system trust stores

options.label: B
options.text: It replaces asymmetric public key infrastructure with symmetric shared secret keys across web browsers

options.label: C
options.text: It allows web servers to deliver timestamped, CA-signed revocation proof during the TLS handshake

options.label: D
options.text: It allows web clients to query multiple Certificate Authorities concurrently to verify root trust chains

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: OCSP Stapling delegates status retrieval to the web server, which caches a signed OCSP response and presents it to connecting clients during TLS negotiation, enhancing speed and privacy.

questions.questionText: Which defense effectively prevents Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing web endpoints?

options.label: A
options.text: Encoding all incoming form parameters into base64 strings before processing them in application controllers

options.label: B
options.text: Validating unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens and using SameSite cookie flags on state-changing requests

options.label: C
options.text: Restricting all backend database transactions to execute in read-only mode for unauthenticated client sessions

options.label: D
options.text: Mandating password complexity rules that enforce credential changes every thirty days for active users

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: CSRF protection requires unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens tied to the user's session that third-party sites cannot read or guess, alongside SameSite cookie attributes.

questions.questionText: What underlying microarchitectural processor mechanism enables Spectre speculative execution side-channel attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: Hardware thermal throttling desynchronizing clock cycles between physical processor execution cores

options.label: B
options.text: Improper cyclic redundancy checks on L1 data cache lines during asynchronous direct memory access

options.label: C
options.text: Branch predictors executing instructions speculatively past bounds checks and leaving cache timing traces

options.label: D
options.text: Memory management unit page table fragmentation allowing unprivileged user space to read kernel frames

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Spectre exploits speculative execution where CPUs predict branch targets and execute code before bounds checks complete. When squashed, cache state changes persist and leak data via timing attacks.

questions.questionText: In modern binary exploitation, what is the primary purpose of Return-Oriented Programming (ROP)?

options.label: A
options.text: To accelerate reverse engineering by translating raw assembly opcodes into structured control flow graphs

options.label: B
options.text: To defeat Data Execution Prevention (W^X / DEP) by chaining existing executable instruction sequences ending in ret

options.label: C
options.text: To defeat Address Space Layout Randomization by brute-forcing fixed virtual memory offsets in running processes

options.label: D
options.text: To execute kernel shellcode by directly corrupting the hardware interrupt descriptor table from user space

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: When memory regions are marked non-executable (DEP/NX), ROP circumvents this by reusing existing snippets of executable binary code ('gadgets') ending in return instructions to build arbitrary logic.

questions.questionText: How is Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) typically defeated during exploit development?

options.label: A
options.text: By corrupting the system real-time clock to desynchronize kernel random number generator initialization

options.label: B
options.text: By transmitting high-volume ICMP echo requests to exhaust kernel socket buffer memory allocations

options.label: C
options.text: By using an information leak vulnerability that reveals a kernel pointer to calculate the randomized base offset

options.label: D
options.text: By modifying system security limits in user space configuration files to exceed kernel allocation limits

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: KASLR randomizes the base memory location of kernel code. Attackers leverage an information disclosure bug that leaks a known kernel function pointer to calculate the base slide offset.

questions.questionText: In Kubernetes, which container configuration enables an attacker to perform a host node breakout?

options.label: A
options.text: Attaching a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler that adjusts pod replica counts based on CPU utilization metrics

options.label: B
options.text: Configuring the pod to resolve DNS through cluster CoreDNS services rather than node-local caching daemons

options.label: C
options.text: Deploying a container image built on minimal Alpine Linux rather than an enterprise Linux distribution

options.label: D
options.text: Running in privileged mode with hostPID and hostNetwork enabled or the host filesystem mounted read-write

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: Privileged containers disable Linux cgroup and namespace isolation. Access to host devices or the root filesystem allows escape via chroot, device access, or cgroup release agent manipulation.

questions.questionText: What condition permits an attacker to perform a Blind Time-Based SQL Injection attack against an API?

options.label: A
options.text: The endpoint returns identical responses regardless of query results, but evaluates injected delay functions

options.label: B
options.text: The database connection pool suffers from connection starvation due to unindexed queries on large tables

options.label: C
options.text: The database server exposes detailed error stack traces and internal schema definitions in HTTP 500 responses

options.label: D
options.text: The application communicates with the database over an unencrypted network connection without TLS verification

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: When an application leaks no data or differential error messages, an attacker injects conditional time-delay commands (like pg_sleep or WAITFOR DELAY) to infer data bit-by-bit from response times.

questions.questionText: In SAML 2.0 implementations, what design flaw enables XML Signature Wrapping (XSW) attacks?

options.label: A
options.text: A mismatch between the XML structure used during signature canonicalization and that interpreted by the app

options.label: B
options.text: A mismatch between schema validation of the assertion and resolution of referenced signed element identifiers

options.label: C
options.text: A mismatch between the XML node validated by the signature verifier and the node consumed by business logic

options.label: D
options.text: A mismatch between namespace resolution during signature verification and resolution during assertion processing

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: XSW exploits architectural discrepancies where signature verification validates an intact assertion, while business logic retrieves user claims from an unsigned, wrapped element elsewhere in the DOM.

questions.questionText: What cryptographic flaw made WPA2's 4-way handshake vulnerable to Key Reinstallation Attacks (KRACK)?

options.label: A
options.text: The authentication server transmitting the master pre-shared key in plaintext beacon frames during discovery

options.label: B
options.text: The wireless controller generating predictable initialization vectors during RC4 stream cipher encapsulation

options.label: C
options.text: The access point using weak Diffie-Hellman primes that allow pre-computation attacks against session keys

options.label: D
options.text: The client reinstalling an in-use pairwise key upon receiving retransmitted Message 3, resetting the packet counter

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: KRACK exploits Message 3 retransmission. When re-received, vulnerable clients reinstall the already active PTK and reset its transmit replay counter (nonce), enabling keystream reuse attacks.

questions.questionText: Why is ML-KEM (Kyber) categorized as lattice-based post-quantum cryptography?

options.label: A
options.text: It employs quantum key distribution channels that leverage photon entanglement to detect eavesdropping on optical lines

options.label: B
options.text: It utilizes super-singular elliptic curve isogenies requiring exponential classical resources to compute path morphisms

options.label: C
options.text: It generates symmetric one-time pads derived from cosmic background radiation sensors embedded in security modules

options.label: D
options.text: Its security relies on high-dimensional lattice vector problems that cannot be solved efficiently by Shor's algorithm

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: ML-KEM security reduces to the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) problem over high-dimensional lattices, which resists both classical algorithms and quantum attacks based on Shor's algorithm.

questions.questionText: In eBPF security observability tooling, how can a root-privileged adversary attempt to blind kernel telemetry?

options.label: A
options.text: By installing unapproved compilers on the host worker node to trigger local static binary analysis warnings

options.label: B
options.text: By detaching kernel tracepoints via bpf syscalls or flooding the ring buffer to induce massive unlogged event drops

options.label: C
options.text: By modifying userspace /etc/resolv.conf configuration files to redirect internal DNS queries to external resolvers

options.label: D
options.text: By adjusting system timezone configurations to create clock drift between worker nodes and the control plane

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: An adversary with root or CAP_BPF can interact directly with the bpf() syscall to detach attached probes, corrupt BPF maps, or generate high-volume synthetic events to overflow ring buffers.

questions.questionText: Which defense mechanism specifically protects cloud instance metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) against SSRF?

options.label: A
options.text: Enforcing multi-factor authentication on all administrative SSH connections established to worker compute nodes

options.label: B
options.text: Configuring public DNS records to map internal private IP subnets to corporate reverse proxy load balancers

options.label: C
options.text: Enforcing IMDSv2 requiring session-oriented PUT requests with signed token headers alongside strict egress filtering

options.label: D
options.text: Encoding all outbound HTTP request bodies into base64 strings before transmitting them over network gateways

questions.explanationAfterAnswer: IMDSv2 requires clients to first execute a PUT request to generate a session token (which standard SSRF vectors cannot easily forge) before querying metadata, and sets token hop limits to block proxies.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What is the primary role of a network firewall in an IT infrastructure?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: To inspect and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
questionBreakdown.correctOption: To inspect and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
questionBreakdown.explanation: A firewall monitors and filters inbound and outbound network traffic based on predefined security rules, acting as a barrier between trusted internal networks and untrusted external networks.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Which of the following best describes 'Multi-Factor Authentication' (MFA)?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Requiring two different people to approve every system login
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Verifying identity using two or more distinct authentication factors (e.g., password + SMS/TOTP token)
questionBreakdown.explanation: MFA requires two or more distinct categories of evidence: something you know (password), something you have (authenticator app/security key), or something you are (biometrics).

questionBreakdown.questionText: What distinguishes symmetric encryption from asymmetric encryption?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Symmetric encryption only works on numbers, whereas asymmetric works on text
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Symmetric encryption uses the same secret key for both encryption and decryption, while asymmetric uses a public/private key pair
questionBreakdown.explanation: Symmetric encryption (like AES) uses a single shared secret key for encryption and decryption. Asymmetric encryption (like RSA or ECC) uses mathematically linked public and private keys.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What type of attack involves an adversary tricking individuals into revealing sensitive credentials via deceptive emails?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: SQL Injection
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Phishing
questionBreakdown.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering attack where attackers impersonate trustworthy entities to deceive victims into opening malicious links or disclosing sensitive credentials.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What does the 'A' in the CIA triad of information security stand for?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Authorization
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Availability
questionBreakdown.explanation: The CIA triad consists of Confidentiality (protecting data from unauthorized access), Integrity (ensuring data is accurate and untampered), and Availability (ensuring systems and data are accessible when needed).

questionBreakdown.questionText: An employee receives an email seemingly from their company CEO demanding an urgent gift card purchase. What practical action should the employee take?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Immediately buy the gift cards to show dedication
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Verify the request through an established out-of-band communication channel like calling the CEO directly
questionBreakdown.explanation: Executive impersonation (Business Email Compromise) relies on artificial urgency. The correct procedure is always out-of-band verification via a known, verified channel.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Why should software applications never store user passwords in plain text inside a database?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: If the database is compromised, all user passwords are immediately exposed to the attacker
questionBreakdown.correctOption: If the database is compromised, all user passwords are immediately exposed to the attacker
questionBreakdown.explanation: Storing plaintext passwords guarantees total account takeover across services if a database leak occurs. Passwords must be hashed using salted, slow cryptographic hash functions (like bcrypt, Argon2).

questionBreakdown.questionText: When browsing the web, what does the padlock icon and 'https://' in the browser address bar indicate?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: The website is completely immune to malware and virus attacks
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Network traffic between your browser and the web server is encrypted via TLS
questionBreakdown.explanation: HTTPS signifies that transport layer encryption (TLS) is active, protecting communication from eavesdropping and tampering in transit. It does not guarantee the server itself is trustworthy or bug-free.

questionBreakdown.questionText: An organization wants to prevent unauthorized wireless devices from connecting to their corporate network. Which method provides the strongest security?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: WPA3 Enterprise with 802.1X certificate-based authentication
questionBreakdown.correctOption: WPA3 Enterprise with 802.1X certificate-based authentication
questionBreakdown.explanation: SSID hiding and MAC filtering are trivial to bypass with basic packet sniffers. WPA3 Enterprise using 802.1X requires individual cryptographic credentials or certificates per device, preventing credential sharing and replay attacks.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What is the primary risk of using default administrative credentials on newly installed network switches and routers?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Network packets will travel at half the rated port speed
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Automated adversary bots scan default ports and gain full administrative control using publicly known vendor passwords
questionBreakdown.explanation: Factory default credentials are systematically cataloged in publicly accessible threat databases. Automated adversary scanners exploit them within minutes of exposure to public or internal networks.

questionBreakdown.questionText: How does a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack execute within a target's web browser?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: By injecting untrusted client-side script into web application output that is executed by other users' browsers
questionBreakdown.correctOption: By injecting untrusted client-side script into web application output that is executed by other users' browsers
questionBreakdown.explanation: XSS occurs when an application includes untrusted user input without proper output encoding, causing the browser to execute malicious JavaScript in the security context of the victim's session.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Which HTTP header is specifically designed to mitigate Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection by restricting where scripts and assets can load from?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Access-Control-Allow-Origin
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
questionBreakdown.explanation: Content-Security-Policy (CSP) allows server administrators to declare approved sources of content (scripts, stylesheets, images) that browsers are permitted to load, blocking inline malicious scripts.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What key difference makes Argon2 or bcrypt vastly superior to SHA-256 for storing user passwords?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Argon2 and bcrypt incorporate configurable computational work factors and memory hardness to resist GPU/ASIC brute-force attacks
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Argon2 and bcrypt incorporate configurable computational work factors and memory hardness to resist GPU/ASIC brute-force attacks
questionBreakdown.explanation: Standard hashing functions like SHA-256 are designed for speed (thousands of mega-hashes per second on GPUs). Password hashing functions must be deliberately slow and memory-hard to render brute-force attacks economically infeasible.

questionBreakdown.questionText: A security analyst notices unexpected outbound DNS queries resolving long random hexadecimal subdomains like 'a1f3c9.attacker-domain.com'. What threat is most likely occurring?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: DNS data exfiltration or Command-and-Control (C2) tunneling
questionBreakdown.correctOption: DNS data exfiltration or Command-and-Control (C2) tunneling
questionBreakdown.explanation: DNS tunneling encodes exfiltrated data or C2 instructions inside DNS query labels because outbound port 53 (DNS) is often left uninspected by egress firewall rules.

questionBreakdown.questionText: How should a development team effectively prevent SQL Injection vulnerabilities across their application services?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) or a trusted ORM that binds parameters separately from query structure
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) or a trusted ORM that binds parameters separately from query structure
questionBreakdown.explanation: Parameterized queries ensure that user input is always treated purely as data, never parsed as executable SQL grammar, making injection structurally impossible.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In a corporate network, what security benefit does implementing network micro-segmentation provide?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: It restricts lateral movement by an attacker if a single workstation or server is compromised
questionBreakdown.correctOption: It restricts lateral movement by an attacker if a single workstation or server is compromised
questionBreakdown.explanation: Micro-segmentation divides workloads into granular security zones with independent access controls, preventing attackers who breach one node from pivoting laterally across the enterprise.

questionBreakdown.questionText: An API uses JWTs for authentication. If the server verifies tokens without enforcing the signature algorithm (e.g., accepting 'alg': 'none'), what attack vector is enabled?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Arbitrary privilege escalation via forged token payloads without cryptographic signing
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Arbitrary privilege escalation via forged token payloads without cryptographic signing
questionBreakdown.explanation: If a JWT parser accepts 'none' as the signature algorithm, an attacker can modify token payload claims (such as 'role': 'admin') and omit the cryptographic signature entirely, bypassing authentication.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What is the primary security objective of implementing the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is required to perform their authorized functions, minimizing blast radius
questionBreakdown.correctOption: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is required to perform their authorized functions, minimizing blast radius
questionBreakdown.explanation: Least Privilege dictates that entities only possess the minimal set of privileges needed for their tasks. When a component is breached, the attacker is constrained by those tight bounds, limiting potential damage.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In public key infrastructure (PKI), how does an Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling mechanism improve upon traditional CRL checking?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: It prevents clients from verifying certificate expiration dates
questionBreakdown.correctOption: It lets the web server provide a timestamped, CA-signed revocation status directly to the client, improving latency and privacy
questionBreakdown.explanation: OCSP stapling has the web server periodically query the CA and attach the signed status to the TLS handshake. This speeds up handshakes and stops the CA from tracking user browsing patterns.

questionBreakdown.correctOption: They incorporate configurable work factors and memory hardness to resist GPU and ASIC brute-force attacks
questionBreakdown.explanation: Fast hash functions like SHA-256 are engineered for speed, allowing billions of guesses per second on GPUs. Adaptive functions introduce computational work factors and memory demands to thwart hardware cracking.

questionBreakdown.questionText: A security analyst observes high volumes of outbound DNS queries for random hex subdomains. What is the threat?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: DNS tunneling and data exfiltration encoding unauthorized data within sequential lookup query labels
questionBreakdown.correctOption: DNS tunneling and data exfiltration encoding unauthorized data within sequential lookup query labels
questionBreakdown.explanation: DNS tunneling encapsulates non-DNS traffic or stolen data inside DNS queries (e.g. data.attacker.com), bypassing standard egress firewall rules that leave port 53 open.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What is the most robust defense against SQL Injection vulnerabilities in modern web applications?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) that separate user input from SQL command structure
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) that separate user input from SQL command structure
questionBreakdown.explanation: Parameterized queries ensure the database driver treats user input strictly as data values, preventing user input from altering the compiled SQL query syntax.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What security advantage does network micro-segmentation provide inside a corporate infrastructure?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: It isolates workloads into discrete zones, preventing adversaries from moving laterally if a host is breached
questionBreakdown.correctOption: It isolates workloads into discrete zones, preventing adversaries from moving laterally if a host is breached
questionBreakdown.explanation: Micro-segmentation restricts communication between workloads according to granular policies, limiting an attacker's ability to move laterally across an internal network.

questionBreakdown.questionText: If an API verifies JWTs without enforcing the signature algorithm (accepting 'alg: none'), what attack occurs?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Attackers can forge arbitrary claims and tamper with tokens without needing a valid cryptographic signature
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Attackers can forge arbitrary claims and tamper with tokens without needing a valid cryptographic signature
questionBreakdown.explanation: If a server blindly honors 'alg: none', an attacker can modify the token payload (e.g. elevating role to admin) and strip the signature, gaining unauthorized privileges.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What is the primary security goal of implementing the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is necessary, minimizing potential blast radius
questionBreakdown.correctOption: To restrict user and process permissions strictly to what is necessary, minimizing potential blast radius
questionBreakdown.explanation: Least Privilege dictates that users, processes, and systems should hold only the bare minimum permissions required to perform their functions, containing damage from compromise.

questionBreakdown.questionText: How does Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling improve upon traditional revocation checking?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: It allows web servers to deliver timestamped, CA-signed revocation proof during the TLS handshake
questionBreakdown.correctOption: It allows web servers to deliver timestamped, CA-signed revocation proof during the TLS handshake
questionBreakdown.explanation: OCSP Stapling delegates status retrieval to the web server, which caches a signed OCSP response and presents it to connecting clients during TLS negotiation, enhancing speed and privacy.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Which defense effectively prevents Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing web endpoints?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Validating unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens and using SameSite cookie flags on state-changing requests
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Validating unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens and using SameSite cookie flags on state-changing requests
questionBreakdown.explanation: CSRF protection requires unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens tied to the user's session that third-party sites cannot read or guess, alongside SameSite cookie attributes.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What underlying microarchitectural processor mechanism enables Spectre speculative execution side-channel attacks?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Branch predictors executing instructions speculatively past bounds checks and leaving cache timing traces
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Branch predictors executing instructions speculatively past bounds checks and leaving cache timing traces
questionBreakdown.explanation: Spectre exploits speculative execution where CPUs predict branch targets and execute code before bounds checks complete. When squashed, cache state changes persist and leak data via timing attacks.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In modern binary exploitation, what is the primary purpose of Return-Oriented Programming (ROP)?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: To defeat Data Execution Prevention (W^X / DEP) by chaining existing executable instruction sequences ending in ret
questionBreakdown.correctOption: To defeat Data Execution Prevention (W^X / DEP) by chaining existing executable instruction sequences ending in ret
questionBreakdown.explanation: When memory regions are marked non-executable (DEP/NX), ROP circumvents this by reusing existing snippets of executable binary code ('gadgets') ending in return instructions to build arbitrary logic.

questionBreakdown.questionText: How is Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) typically defeated during exploit development?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: By using an information leak vulnerability that reveals a kernel pointer to calculate the randomized base offset
questionBreakdown.correctOption: By using an information leak vulnerability that reveals a kernel pointer to calculate the randomized base offset
questionBreakdown.explanation: KASLR randomizes the base memory location of kernel code. Attackers leverage an information disclosure bug that leaks a known kernel function pointer to calculate the base slide offset.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In Kubernetes, which container configuration enables an attacker to perform a host node breakout?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Running in privileged mode with hostPID and hostNetwork enabled or the host filesystem mounted read-write
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Running in privileged mode with hostPID and hostNetwork enabled or the host filesystem mounted read-write
questionBreakdown.explanation: Privileged containers disable Linux cgroup and namespace isolation. Access to host devices or the root filesystem allows escape via chroot, device access, or cgroup release agent manipulation.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What condition permits an attacker to perform a Blind Time-Based SQL Injection attack against an API?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: The endpoint returns identical responses regardless of query results, but evaluates injected delay functions
questionBreakdown.correctOption: The endpoint returns identical responses regardless of query results, but evaluates injected delay functions
questionBreakdown.explanation: When an application leaks no data or differential error messages, an attacker injects conditional time-delay commands (like pg_sleep or WAITFOR DELAY) to infer data bit-by-bit from response times.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In SAML 2.0 implementations, what design flaw enables XML Signature Wrapping (XSW) attacks?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: A mismatch between the XML node validated by the signature verifier and the node consumed by business logic
questionBreakdown.correctOption: A mismatch between the XML node validated by the signature verifier and the node consumed by business logic
questionBreakdown.explanation: XSW exploits architectural discrepancies where signature verification validates an intact assertion, while business logic retrieves user claims from an unsigned, wrapped element elsewhere in the DOM.

questionBreakdown.questionText: What cryptographic flaw made WPA2's 4-way handshake vulnerable to Key Reinstallation Attacks (KRACK)?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: The client reinstalling an in-use pairwise key upon receiving retransmitted Message 3, resetting the packet counter
questionBreakdown.correctOption: The client reinstalling an in-use pairwise key upon receiving retransmitted Message 3, resetting the packet counter
questionBreakdown.explanation: KRACK exploits Message 3 retransmission. When re-received, vulnerable clients reinstall the already active PTK and reset its transmit replay counter (nonce), enabling keystream reuse attacks.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Why is ML-KEM (Kyber) categorized as lattice-based post-quantum cryptography?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Its security relies on high-dimensional lattice vector problems that cannot be solved efficiently by Shor's algorithm
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Its security relies on high-dimensional lattice vector problems that cannot be solved efficiently by Shor's algorithm
questionBreakdown.explanation: ML-KEM security reduces to the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) problem over high-dimensional lattices, which resists both classical algorithms and quantum attacks based on Shor's algorithm.

questionBreakdown.questionText: In eBPF security observability tooling, how can a root-privileged adversary attempt to blind kernel telemetry?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: By detaching kernel tracepoints via bpf syscalls or flooding the ring buffer to induce massive unlogged event drops
questionBreakdown.correctOption: By detaching kernel tracepoints via bpf syscalls or flooding the ring buffer to induce massive unlogged event drops
questionBreakdown.explanation: An adversary with root or CAP_BPF can interact directly with the bpf() syscall to detach attached probes, corrupt BPF maps, or generate high-volume synthetic events to overflow ring buffers.

questionBreakdown.questionText: Which defense mechanism specifically protects cloud instance metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) against SSRF?
questionBreakdown.selectedOption: Configuring public DNS records to map internal private IP subnets to corporate reverse proxy load balancers
questionBreakdown.correctOption: Enforcing IMDSv2 requiring session-oriented PUT requests with signed token headers alongside strict egress filtering
questionBreakdown.explanation: IMDSv2 requires clients to first execute a PUT request to generate a session token (which standard SSRF vectors cannot easily forge) before querying metadata, and sets token hop limits to block proxies.

assessmentQuestions.questionText: "Kshnabhangurvada" is the doctrine of which philosopher?

options.label: A
options.text: Shankaracharya

options.label: B
options.text: Buddha

options.label: C
options.text: Kapila

options.label: D
options.text: Gautama

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Kshanabhanguravada (theory of momentariness/impermanence) is a cardinal doctrine in Buddhist philosophy propounded by Gautama Buddha.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Padartha Vijnana & Ayurveda Itihasa
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4001

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Snigdha, (B) Yukti, (C) Sukha, (D) Gandha
List II: (I) Buddhyadi Guna, (II) Gurvadi Guna, (III) Shabdadi Guna, (IV) Paradi Guna
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Padartha Vijnana: Snigdha is among the Gurvadi gunas (20 sharira gunas), Yukti is among the Paradi gunas, Sukha is among the Atma/Buddhyadi gunas, and Gandha is a Vaisheshika/Shabdadi guna.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Padartha Vijnana
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4002

assessmentQuestions.questionText: Which combination (Sandhi) is in word 'हृद्यौषधम्' (Hridyaushadham)?

options.label: A
options.text: Vriddhi

options.label: B
options.text: Yana

options.label: C
options.text: Ayadi

options.label: D
options.text: Guna

assessmentQuestions.explanation: In Sanskrit grammar, Hridya + Aushadham = Hridyaushadham (a + au = au), which is an example of Vriddhi Sandhi according to Panini sutra 'Vriddhiradaich'.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Sanskrit & Ayurveda Samhita
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4003

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
According to Sushruta consider two statements as given below:
Statement I: Ojasa is a Sara of Shukra.
Statement II: 'Sandhivishlesha' is the feature of Ojakshaya.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Sushruta Samhita Sutrasthana 15, Ojas is described as the essence/sarabhaga of all dhatus terminating with Shukra ('Ojaastu tejodhatunam...'). Furthermore, 'Sandhivishlesha' (looseness of joints) is a classic clinical lakshana of Ojakshaya/Ojasvisramsa.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Kriya Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4004

assessmentQuestions.questionText: According to Sushruta 'धैर्य' (Dhairya), is the function of which one of the following dhatu?

options.label: A
options.text: Mamsa

options.label: B
options.text: Asthi

options.label: C
options.text: Majja

options.label: D
options.text: Shukra

assessmentQuestions.explanation: In Sushruta Samhita Sutrasthana chapter 15, the specific function of Shukra dhatu is defined as 'धैर्यं च्यवनं प्रीतिर्देहबलं हर्षो बीजार्य च' (dhairya, chyavana, priti, dehabala, harsha, and bijartha).
assessmentQuestions.subject: Kriya Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4005

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Match List I with List II (According to Sushruta types of Vata and its properties/karma):
List I (Vayu): (A) Vyana, (B) Udana, (C) Samana, (D) Apana
List II (Karma): (I) Udvahana, (II) Dharana, (III) Praspandana, (IV) Viveka
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Sushruta Samhita: Vyana vata performs Praspandana (pulsation/circulation), Udana performs Udvahana, Samana performs Viveka (sorting/digestion separation), and Apana performs Dharana (retention/downward expulsion).
assessmentQuestions.subject: Kriya Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4006

assessmentQuestions.questionText: How many types of Nidraa has been described by Ashtanga Sangraha?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Acharya Vagbhata in Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana chapter 9 describes 7 varieties of Nidra (sleep): Kalasvabhava, Tamobhava, Kaphaja, Sharirasramajanya, Manasramajanya, Agantuki, and Vyadhyanuvartini.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Swasthavritta & Kriya Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4007

assessmentQuestions.questionText: Which Bhava is responsible for 'Indriya Prasada'?

options.label: A
options.text: Rasaja Bhava

options.label: B
options.text: Satmyaja Bhava

options.label: C
options.text: Satvaja Bhava

options.label: D
options.text: Matrija Bhava

assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Charaka Samhita Sharirasthana 3/11, Satmyaja Bhavas include Arogya, Analasatva, Aloluptva, Indriya Prasada, Svara-Varna-Bija Sampat, and Praharsha.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Rachana & Kriya Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4008

assessmentQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a content of femoral sheath?

options.label: A
options.text: Femoral artery

options.label: B
options.text: Femoral nerve

options.label: C
options.text: Femoral vein

options.label: D
options.text: Femoral canal

assessmentQuestions.explanation: The femoral sheath encloses the femoral artery (lateral compartment), femoral vein (intermediate compartment), and femoral canal (medial compartment). The femoral nerve lies outside and lateral to the femoral sheath in the femoral triangle.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Rachana Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4009

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Sushruta has mentioned 'Kala' in this order:
(A) Purishadhara kala
(B) Shleshmodhara kala
(C) Pittadhara kala
(D) Mamsadhara kala
(E) Raktadhara kala
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Sushruta Samhita Sharirasthana 4 describes 7 Kalas sequentially: 1st Mamsadhara (D), 2nd Raktadhara (E), 3rd Medodhara, 4th Shleshmodhara (B), 5th Purishadhara (A), 6th Pittadhara (C), and 7th Sukradhara. Hence the sequence is (D), (E), (B), (A), (C).
assessmentQuestions.subject: Rachana Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4010

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Which of the following Marma are 'Kalantar Pranahara'?
(A) Lohitaksha
(B) Bruhati
(C) Ansaphalaka
(D) Katikataruna
(E) Guda
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.label: A
options.text: (A), (C) and (E) only

options.label: B
options.text: (B), (C) and (E) only

options.label: C
options.text: (A), (D) only

options.label: D
options.text: (B), (D) only

assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Sushruta Marma Sharira, Bruhati and Katikataruna are classified as Kalantara Pranahara Marmas (which cause death after a period of time). Lohitaksha is Vaikalyakara, Ansaphalaka is Vaikalyakara, and Guda is Sadyah Pranahara.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Shalya Tantra & Rachana Sharira
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4011

assessmentQuestions.questionText: According to Ashtanga Hridaya in which of the following disease Sleep is prohibited during night time?

options.label: A
options.text: Indigestion

options.label: B
options.text: Throat disease

options.label: C
options.text: Diarrhoea

options.label: D
options.text: Abdominal pain

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Ashtanga Hridaya Sutrasthana 7 forbids sleep during the night in throat diseases (Kantharoga) because lying down and nocturnal kapha accumulation aggravates upper airway obstruction and complications.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Swasthavritta & Shalakya Tantra
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4012

assessmentQuestions.questionText: The Lekhan Anjana is prepared from which of the following type of drugs?

options.label: A
options.text: Drugs having Bitter taste and hot potency

options.label: B
options.text: Drugs having Sweet taste and cold potency

options.label: C
options.text: Drugs having Astringent, sour and salt taste

options.label: D
options.text: Drugs having Pungent, Bitter and Astringent taste

assessmentQuestions.explanation: According to Shalakya Tantra and Sushruta Samhita, Lekhana Anjana (scraping/depletive collyrium) is prepared using dravyas predominantly having Katu (pungent), Tikta (bitter), and Kashaya (astringent) rasas along with Ushna veerya.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Shalakya Tantra
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4013

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Given below are two statements as per Charak Samhita:
Statement I: 'Nidrabaladihani' is mentioned as one of the lakshana of Vamana Atiyoga.
Statement II: 'Nidrabalabhava' is mentioned as one of the lakshana of Virechana Atiyoga.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

assessmentQuestions.explanation: In Charaka Samhita Siddhisthana chapter 1, excessive evacuation (Atiyoga) of Vamana produces Nidra-bala-hani along with giddiness and dehydration; Virechana Atiyoga similarly leads to depletion of sleep and strength (Nidrabalabhava). Both statements are classically accurate.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Panchakarma
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4014

assessmentQuestions.questionText: Botanical name of herb 'Nidigdhika' is —

options.label: A
options.text: Curcuma longa

options.label: B
options.text: Curcuma augustifolia

options.label: C
options.text: Solanum surattense

options.label: D
options.text: Solanum nigrum

assessmentQuestions.explanation: Nidigdhika (also known as Kantakari / Vyaghri) is botanically identified as Solanum surattense Burm. f. (syn. Solanum xanthocarpum Schrad. & Wendl.), belonging to the family Solanaceae.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Dravyaguna Vijnana
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4015

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
Match List I with List II:
List I - (Dravya): (A) Tila, (B) Japa, (C) Padmaka, (D) Gokshura
List II - (Family): (I) Malvaceae, (II) Zygophyllaceae, (III) Rosaceae, (IV) Pedaliaceae
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Tila (Sesamum indicum) belongs to Pedaliaceae (IV); Japa (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) belongs to Malvaceae (I); Padmaka (Prunus cerasoides) belongs to Rosaceae (III); Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) belongs to Zygophyllaceae (II).
assessmentQuestions.subject: Dravyaguna Vijnana
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4016

assessmentQuestions.questionText: "Rasai Rasou Tulyafalah" (रसै रसौ तुल्यफलः) is described for which of the following Dravyagata Padartha by Ashtanga Sangraha?

options.label: A
options.text: Karma

options.label: B
options.text: Guna

options.label: C
options.text: Veerya

options.label: D
options.text: Vipaaka

assessmentQuestions.explanation: In Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana chapter 17, Vipaka is described as yielding effects parallel to the respective tastes: 'रसै रसौ तुल्यफलः' indicating that Vipaka action aligns with Rasas unless Vikriti Vishama Samaveta.
assessmentQuestions.subject: Dravyaguna Vijnana
assessmentQuestions.sourceRef: NSEIT AIAPGET 2025 Ayurveda QP, Client Question ID 4017

assessmentQuestions.questionText: A patient comes to an OPD with complaints of Diarrhoea with indigested food particles and mucus. He has diagnosed with Apakwa Atisaar. Which action is required to treat the condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Grahi

options.label: B
options.text: Stambhana

options.label: C
options.text: Sandhaneeya

options.label: D
options.text: Pureeshvirajaneeya

assessmentQuestions.questionText:
